knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A damp cloth captures dust, and working top to bottom stops dust falling onto surfaces already cleaned.
Spray creates a fine mist that can irritate and spread material; a squeeze bottle or a cloth gives much less mist.
The standard calls for HEPA filters and regular filter changes as part of scheduled maintenance.
The dust control section says tools that stir dust into the air, such as brooms and feather dusters, should be avoided in healthcare areas.

practicalCriteria: Learner dusts a sample surface using a damp cloth top to bottom, with no dry dusting and no spray into the air
Learner identifies the filter and bag condition on a sample vacuum and states whether it can be used
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the dusting exercise
stopWorkCriteria: A vacuum has a damaged bag or unknown filter and is for use near a clinical area
Spray product is being used while patients are in the room, with no ventilation
